assessment.reason: The model's large edge over a 10-book consensus is not explained by its displayed drivers, so the price case rests on an unexplained road-favorite margin.
assessment.model_case: The model projects the Dodgers by about 1.4 runs on the road. Its displayed inputs do not show where that comes from: Milwaukee has the better recent scoring, the starters' recent RA/9 is essentially identical, and Milwaukee has home field. Unseen features would have to carry the entire margin, and none is shown.
assessment.price_case: At -128 the break-even sits only slightly above the paired 10-book market, while the model sits well above both. The 0.25-weight blend leaves only a thin margin. Ten books agreeing near break-even is broad pricing, and the model disagrees with it without a visible reason.
assessment.context_case: The starter matchup appears to match the model. Dodgers relief absences listed in the snapshot may thin late-inning depth. It is unknown whether the model or the market already reflects those absences.

qualitative_review.countercase: The Dodgers' overall talent may justify a larger edge than recent run rates suggest, and Yamamoto's postseason form may be underpriced.

assessment.model_case: Recent volume of about 14.4 outs per start sits above 13.5, but the projection is under 14, only half an out above the line. findings.note: The Brewers' bullpen held a 2-1 Game 1 win over LA. Milwaukee is only the fourth team to open a postseason with five straight games decided by two runs or fewer, a bad sign for a -1.5 cover. Logan Henderson starts Game 2.
Says offense is at a premium this postseason. The Dodgers are just 2-for-27 with runners in scoring position, which points to low scoring and close games rather than a two-run road win.

Game 2 pitchers: Yamamoto (1-0, 1.29 ERA over 7 postseason innings) vs Henderson (1.80 ERA over 5 innings). Milwaukee went 55-26 at home and had MLB's best record at 103-59. Forecast is 83 degrees in Milwaukee; the park has a roof.
CBS/RotoWire (Oct 11) confirms Rasmussen will start ALCS Game 1 against Cleveland, and says he struck out 10 Yankees over eight scoreless innings in his last start, the ALDS opener.

MLB.com says Rasmussen is fully rested and the Rays have won his last 13 starts. He struck out nine Guardians over seven scoreless innings on July 26. Cash said he hopes Rasmussen comes close to his ALDS outing, though the writer says that may not be realistic.
In his other 2026 start against Cleveland (April 29), Rasmussen struck out six over five innings, which also clears 5.5. No reported injury or pitch limit was found that would favor the Under.
